notes:
All four preprod findings for get_test_case_history_v1 REPRODUCE on prod (verdict: DRIFT), confirmed against real production data.

1) version_name — REPRODUCES. Diffed the exact same history_id both ways: in the get_test_case_histories_v1 LISTING (project 332537, test_case 30883570, p=1), history_id 139972066 carries "version_name":"V4" and history_id 7321851 carries "version_name":"V2". Calling get_test_case_history_v1 for those SAME two history_ids returns a history object with no version_name key at all (not null — absent) in both cases. The schema declares version_name as a nullable string on the single-read response, so this is a genuine declared-vs-actual gap, and it is the specific 'listing carries it for the same id, single-read drops it' pattern called out from preprod.

2) user.email — REPRODUCES. The schema's nested `user` sub-schema declares an `email` field. Both single-reads (history_id 139972066 and 7321851) return a `user` object with id/browserstack_user_id/full_name/group_id/onboarded/reports_and_notification_enabled but no `email` key. Same gap as on the listing capability.

3) origin_channel — REPRODUCES as 'present but undeclared', though the concrete value differs from preprod. Preprod's single-read showed `origin_channel: "api"`; on this prod record (history_id 139972066, an update made via the web UI) it is `origin_channel: "ui"`, and on an older 2025-04 record (history_id 7321851) it is `null`. In all cases the field is returned and is absent from the declared schema (declared_missing list for the `history` object has no origin_channel property) — undeclared_returned confirmed, value is channel-dependent (api vs ui) rather than a fixed string.

4) Redundancy/enrichment pattern — REPRODUCES exactly. For the FIRST/newest row on the page (history_id 139972066, V4): the get_test_case_histories_v1 listing already returned the full `modified` map for `automation_status` (old/new) inline — this route's own guidance says the listing only enriches the first record per page, and that held true here. Fetching the single-entry read for that same first row added no new field data and was strictly worse: it dropped `version_name` (finding #1) while gaining nothing. For a NON-first row (history_id 7321851, V2, third of four): the listing gave only `modified_fields: ["template","preconditions","test_case_steps"]` — field names with no values. The single-read for that id returned the full old/new `modified` map, including the complete 8-step `test_case_steps` array (old: null, new: [8 step objects]) and the full `preconditions` text. That is exactly the valuable case for this route.

Deviation from the prescribed setup, and why: the task named TC-838571/TC-838570/TC-838569 (folder 9697326) as the source for 'richest trail' — but get_test_case_histories_v1 against all three (recorded in setup step 1) showed each has exactly ONE history row (a bare 'create', count=1, no edits ever recorded). None of the three folder-9697326 cases could supply a first-row-vs-non-first-row comparison because none has a second row. To honestly test finding #4 (and to re-confirm #1–#3 against a genuinely multi-revision record, since a single 'create' row has no modified_fields/modified to compare), I searched project 332537 read-only (get_test_cases_v1 project-wide, then get_test_case_histories_v1 on a few candidates) and found TC-829017 (integer id 30883570, folder 'payment flow') with 4 real revisions spanning 2025-04-15 to 2026-09-15. This is an ordinary prod demo-project test case, not one created by this campaign; only read capabilities were invoked against it, nothing was modified. All four preprod findings were verified against it and reproduced.
